questions.stem: Match the CONVENTION with its PRIMARY concern. A. Ramsar. B. CITES. C. Basel. D. Stockholm. List-II: 1. Hazardous-waste trans-boundary movement. 2. Persistent Organic Pollutants. 3. Wetlands of international importance. 4. International trade in endangered species.
questions.explanation: Ramsar (1971, Iran) — wetlands. CITES (1973, Washington DC) — trade in endangered species. Basel (1989) — transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Stockholm (2001) — persistent organic pollutants (POPs like DDT, PCBs, dioxins).

questions.stem: Consider the following about the PARIS AGREEMENT (2015). 1. Each Party submits Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) which are internationally binding emission targets. 2. The long-term goal is to keep the global temperature rise well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. 3. The agreement entered into force in November 2016. 4. Developed countries are obliged to provide at least USD 100 billion per year in climate finance, a goal extended to 2025 at COP26 Glasgow. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is WRONG — NDCs are self-determined and internationally communicated but NOT legally binding as to achievement (only the reporting/updating is binding). This is the famous 'bottom-up' design of Paris. Statements 2, 3, 4 are correct.

questions.stem: The MONTREAL PROTOCOL (1987) is notable for:

options.option_text: First global agreement on greenhouse-gas emissions
Universal ratification and successful phase-out of ozone-depleting substances
Covering only industrialised nations, excluding developing ones

questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol is the ONLY UN treaty with universal (198 party) ratification, and it successfully phased out CFCs and related ODS. The 2016 KIGALI AMENDMENT extended its scope to HFCs (powerful greenhouse gases) — but the core protocol was about ozone, not climate.

questions.stem: India's COMMITMENT under Paris NDCs (updated 2022) INCLUDES:

options.option_text: Reducing emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels by 2030
Achieving 50% cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel resources by 2030

questions.explanation: All three are India's updated NDC commitments. 45 % intensity reduction vs 2005 (earlier 33-35 %). 50 % non-fossil installed capacity by 2030. Net-zero by 2070 (announced at COP26 Glasgow 2021). Also: create additional 2.5-3 billion tonnes of CO2-equivalent carbon sink via additional forest and tree cover by 2030.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): Ocean acidification is a direct consequence of rising atmospheric CO₂ levels. REASON (R): A fraction of the CO₂ absorbed by seawater forms carbonic acid, which releases H⁺ ions, lowering the ocean's pH.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + H⁺. The H⁺ release drops pH. Ocean pH has fallen from ~8.2 (pre-industrial) to ~8.1 today — a ~30 % increase in acidity (pH is logarithmic). Damages coral reefs and shell-forming plankton (pteropods), with cascading effects on marine food webs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of India's 18 BIOSPHERE RESERVES?
questions.explanation: Gir (Gujarat) is a National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary famous for Asiatic lions — but it is NOT one of India's 18 designated Biosphere Reserves. Nilgiri (first designated, 1986), Sundarbans, and Great Nicobar are all Biosphere Reserves under the Indian government programme (and on the UNESCO MAB network).

questions.stem: Consider the following about the KYOTO PROTOCOL (1997). 1. It introduced legally binding emission reduction targets for developed (Annex I) countries for the first commitment period 2008-2012. 2. It was based on the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR). 3. The United States signed but never ratified it. 4. The Doha Amendment extended the Protocol to a second commitment period 2013-2020. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Kyoto's binding targets (5.2 % below 1990 levels overall) distinguished it from later bottom-up Paris. CBDR is a core principle of climate governance. US (Clinton) signed 1998 but Senate refused to ratify (Byrd-Hagel resolution, S. Res. 98). Doha Amendment (2012) covered 2013-2020; ratified slowly, with patchy participation — Paris Agreement took over from 2020.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY cause of the 'ozone hole' phenomenon over Antarctica?

options.option_text: Direct emission of ground-level ozone from industry
Chlorine atoms released from chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) catalytically destroying stratospheric O₃ in the polar vortex
Lightning that breaks down oxygen molecules

questions.explanation: Polar stratospheric clouds provide a surface for heterogeneous reactions; when the Antarctic spring sun arrives, Cl (and Br) radicals released from CFCs catalytically destroy ozone. The polar vortex keeps these reactions concentrated over the pole. Recovery expected ~2060s thanks to Montreal Protocol. Ground-level ozone (a pollutant) is a different story from stratospheric ozone (a protective shield).
